item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Tara looks at the diagram of parallelogram $ABCD$. She measures $\angle DAB = 68^{\circ}$ and $\angle ABC = 112^{\circ}$ and notices the opposite angles match in this drawing. She wonders whether opposite angles of every parallelogram are equal.

Which claim correctly decides what her measurements justify?

options.A: The matching angles in this one drawing prove the property for every parallelogram.
options.B: Equal opposite angles are what create the parallelogram sides in the diagram.
options.C: The measurements support the pattern in this parallelogram; a general property still needs geometric reasoning from known facts.
options.D: Any four-sided shape on the page has equal opposite angles once two angles are measured.
